chunks: Those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers and wish to differentiate between Allah and His messengers, and say: 'We believe in some and disbelieve in others,' and wish to take a way in between,
ai.seo_question: What do the hypocrites mean when they say they believe in some prophets and reject others?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the hypocrites of Medina who selectively accepted prophets to maintain political leverage, foreshadowing the concept of *Tawassul* and the unity of divine authority through the Ahl al-Bayt. It emphasizes that true faith requires accepting all messengers as a cohesive whole, rejecting any artificial separation between Allah and His chosen representatives. This selective belief is viewed as a precursor to the broader theological error of fragmenting the unity of prophethood.
